learningObjectives.text: Explain this episode: Who asks the Achaeans to release his daughter?
Use the cited passage to explain: Why does the plague become an army-wide problem?

main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Chryses offers ransom for his captive daughter. Agamemnon refuses him; Apollo sends plague, and the army must confront the cost of its leader’s decision.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “people, because the son of Atreus had dishonoured Chryses his priest. Now Chryses had come to the ships of the Achaeans to free his daughter, and had brought with him a great ransom: moreover he bore in his hand the sceptre of Apollo wreathed with a suppliant’s wreath, and he besought the Achaeans, but”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: The episode makes honor social rather than private: Agamemnon has power, but he cannot wound a sacred obligation without cost.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Follow the causal sequence: Chryses petitions, Agamemnon refuses, Apollo sends plague. The army suffers for a decision made by its leader; this is more than a private disagreement.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Watch how the poem keeps returning to ransom, gift, and public recognition.

quiz.prompt: Who asks the Achaeans to release his daughter?
quiz.explanation: Chryses. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

quiz.prompt: Why does the plague become an army-wide problem?

choices.text: The ransom has been paid to the wrong king.
Agamemnon’s insult to Apollo’s priest brings divine punishment.
